correctness.rationale: For λ>0, δ≥0 set a=λδ², A=1+a, D=λ+a. Scaled Euler second moments evolve by symmetric nonnegative T=[[α²,2ha],[2ha,β²]] and forcing 2h(1,λ); offdiagonal multiplier αβ−2ha obeys |·|≤ρ(T). The first Perron crossing rho(T)=1 occurs at h*=(A+D−sqrt((A−D)²+4a²))/(AD), including a=0 boundary. For 0<h<h*, a contractive affine random recursion has unique finite-variance invariant law; its covariance is diag(u_h,v_h), with u_h,v_h from exact 2x2 inversion and both >1 from target defect h²(A²,D²). Above threshold Perron projection forces moments from zero to diverge, forbidding any finite-variance stationary law. Strong δ→∞ h*~(1+λ)/(λ²δ⁴); at a=1, λ→0, h*→(3−sqrt5)/2. Independent rational case λ=1/4,a=1,h=1/10: u=91/71,v=464/355, rho≈0.912444. Not a statement about almost-sure instability or stationary Gaussianity.
